original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: For every n>=2 and finite R>=W, formal F2[S_n], paid adjacent transpositions with any binary rank-one scalar idempotent and free GL_R(F2) mixing: prove or refute that the exact cost of diag([w_1],...,[w_W],1,...) equals the sum of inversion counts. Every input is arbitrary and every spectator is restored.
scope_change_reason: Replaces the abelian rational address group with the explicit nonabelian S_n adjacent-transposition alphabet; generalizes the fixed S4 cases of PR1720/1734/1749/1801 using an ordered-pair cut, rather than another finite word search.
bottleneck_link: Scoped obstruction for a proposed bit alphabet. If direct inversion cost is optimal even in the free-scalar relaxation, extra dirty roles cannot give a paid-call saving in this alphabet. No physical BIT supplier or new kappa follows.
stop_rule: One approximately 60-minute session. Falsify the ordered-pair crossing lemma first; if it fails, retain the exact counterexample and stop. Reserve final quarter for independent verification and handoff.
evidence: PROOF.md: written all-n/all-R theorem; verify.py and fixed EXPECTED.json: exact finite coefficients/cuts; independent.py: separately implemented Cayley BFS/full formal operators; test_verify.py: six failure-sensitive tests. REVIEW.md records independent review and exact source hashes.
author: Ross Richardson with OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, with project math-bit-suppliers and independent math-exact-circuit-verification specialists.

open_questions.question: For S4 adjacent-label prices (1,2,1), is the optimal complete dirty-register tariff additive across every ordered target pair?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Different recursive labels may carry different prices; the uniform-price theorem does not prove a weighted no-sharing bound.
open_questions.first_step: Compute direct weighted Cayley distances exactly, then test rational combinations of permutation-action cut inequalities on all 576 target pairs before attempting word synthesis.
open_questions.blocked_by: A matching weighted lower bound or a complete formal sharing counterexample; no physical supplier is identified.

selection_note: The first selector invocation was embedded in oversized output and its result was truncated before the task was read. One recovery invocation was saved before inspection; its bit-mechanisms assignment is used without further draws.
optimistic_budget: Direct bill sum_i inv(w_i); scalar mixing and extra dirty role storage are free in this formal relaxation, while every paid label including restoration costs one. The proposed lower bound matches the complete attaining word.
method: Ordered-pair permutation cut; all-parameter written proof plus exact complete small permutation censuses, full formal dirty circuits and independent checker.
finite_domain: All S_n permutations for 2<=n<=7; all binary rank-one idempotents through R=4 at small n; bounded full formal words and S4 predecessor targets; larger deterministic fixtures.
